subject: Scalable packaging + usage-trigger framework for mid-cycle expansion
messages:
From: Alex Singh <alex.singh@clearpathhealth.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com
Cc: megan.liu@clearpathhealth.com
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Looking for a way to scale mid-contract (capacity + spend predictability)

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team liked the throughput and the latency numbers. We just finished a product review and are looking at a mid-cycle expansion: roughly 2.5x token volume for 3–6 months starting in January. Primary asks from procurement and engineering:

- Can we avoid a full annual uplift commitment?
- Is there a way to get predictable unit pricing while allowing for surges?
- Any concessions for a short-term capacity burst (we'd pay for consumed tokens, but want some discount banding)?

Megan (cc'd) will be the procurement lead. Can you send a short outline of options and what paperwork/procurement steps you need?

Cheers,
Alex
Alex Singh
Head of Integrations, Clearpath Health
alex.singh@clearpathhealth.com
+1 415-555-0192
From: jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com
To: Alex Singh <alex.singh@clearpathhealth.com>
Cc: Megan Liu <megan.liu@clearpathhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Looking for a way to scale mid-contract (capacity + spend predictability)

Alex / Megan — thanks for the note and great to hear the demo resonated. High level options we typically propose for a predictable, scalable expansion without forcing a full-year uplift:

1) Rolling surge buffer + consumption discount
   - Keep your current committed bucket. Add a short-term surge buffer (prepaid or reserved) that unlocks a stepped discount as consumption hits defined triggers.
   - Example: first +50% consumption at list price, next +100% consumption at 12% discount, any incremental above that at 18% discount.

2) Short-term committed tranche (6-month term)
   - If you can commit to a 6-month tranche for the incremental capacity, we can offer a blended discount across that tranche and the base commitment. This avoids an annual amendment.

3) Flexible co-term addendum + auto-fallback
   - Add a short amendment that co-terms with existing renewal but includes an automatic fallback to hosted lower-cost variants if usage drops. Limits risk for both sides.

I'll attach a concise proposal and a simple calculator so you can play with trigger thresholds. Operationally we need: a PO or signed addendum for any prepaid surge buffer, and a quick procurement contact for DocuSign.

I'm looping in Ben and Naomi internally for pricing and any finance constraints. Quick ask: are there any SSO/contract signatory timing constraints on your side before Jan?

Best,
Jonas Weber
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com
From: jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com
To: ben_carter@redwoodinference.com, naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com, lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 10:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Clearpath — mid-cycle expansion asks (pricing input)

Team — forwarding Clearpath's ask. Key points: 2.5x volume for 3–6 months, prefer not to do full annual uplift, want predictable unit pricing with surge protection.

My proposal above (buffer + triggers, or 6-month tranche). Questions for pricing/finance:
- Feasibility of the stepped discount (12% then 18%) for incremental usage bands?
- Are we comfortable with a prepaid surge buffer claimable against true consumption (i.e., customer buys $X of burst credits)?
- Any redlines from legal we should preempt on a 6-month addendum?

I suggest we package two clean options for procurement (one consumption-first, one commit-first) and a one‑pager of operational steps (PO -> DocuSign -> activation).

Thanks,
Jonas

-- Forwarded message --
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com, naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com, lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 08 Dec 2026 13:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Clearpath — mid-cycle expansion asks (pricing input)

Jonas — read this. Finance and I are OK with a structure that preserves existing committed economics while giving Clearpath a path to predictable unit pricing for incremental consumption. My notes / guardrails:

- Stepped discount is fine, populate exact bands in the calculator. Suggested bands: 0–1.5x = list, 1.5–3.0x = 12% off, >3.0x = 20% off (moves our earlier numbers slightly to protect margin).
- Prepaid surge buffer OK, but we require a minimum buffer purchase of $25k and the buffer expires at the end of the burst window (no refunds). This keeps revenue recognition clean.
- For the 6-month tranche, finance needs a signed addendum (DocuSign) and an estimate of expected committed tokens to size the tranche. We can offer a blended 14% discount on the tranche if the tranche >= $150k net new ARR equivalent.
- Legal: standard short addendum template is okay; avoid long-term price guarantees beyond the tranche window. Finance will approve as long as terms above are enforced.

Naomi — can you run margin sensitivity with these bands (I included the calculator in the draft attachments). Lauren — happy to review the one-pager and procurement steps.

Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
From: jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com
To: Alex Singh <alex.singh@clearpathhealth.com>, Megan Liu <megan.liu@clearpathhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Dec 2026 16:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Proposal: two-path expansion (consumption buffer OR 6-month tranche) — Clearpath Health

Alex / Megan — apologies for the delay; attached are two concise options we discussed: a consumption-first path (prepaid surge buffer + stepped discounts) and a commit-first path (6-month tranche with blended pricing). Summary below and attached: scalable-packaging-proposal-v1.pdf; usage-trigger-calculator.xlsx.

Option A — Consumption-first (prepaid buffer + triggers)
- Minimum prepaid buffer: $25,000 (usable against surges beginning Jan 1)
- Discount bands: 0–1.5x = list; 1.5–3.0x = 12% off; >3.0x = 20% off
- Buffer expires at end of the agreed burst window (90 days unless we agree to 180).
- Operational steps: PO -> DocuSign addendum -> activate buffer

Option B — Commit-first (6-month tranche)
- Commit to an incremental tranche sized to expected usage for 6 months
- Blended discount for the tranche: 14% if tranche >= $150k net new ARR equivalent
- Tranche co-terms with existing renewal; standard addendum, immediate activation on signature

Next steps:
1) If you prefer Option A, confirm buffer size and window (90 vs 180 days).
2) If Option B, share an estimate for the tranche size and we'll route DocuSign.
3) I can run a quick forecast for internal approvals if you share expected weekly token throughput.

Happy to jump on a 30-min call this week to finalize.

Best regards,
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com
